hypothesis: Lower idle cash in non-stress states may raise return without breaking defense.
success_criteria: Return improves with drawdown above -22% and Sharpe >= 0.85.
kill_criteria: Reject if return remains near Track A or stress drawdown deteriorates materially.

hypothesis: More targeted cash reduction in good states may improve return with less neutral-state risk.
success_criteria: Return improves and 2x cost Sharpe remains >= 0.85.
kill_criteria: Reject if neutral-state losses dominate the improvement.

hypothesis: A stronger cash cap tests whether 9% return is reachable without stress changes.
success_criteria: CAGR approaches 9% with max drawdown above -22%.
kill_criteria: Reject if drawdown or CVaR worsens faster than return improves.

hypothesis: Small offense scaling may lift return while retaining Track A state timing.
success_criteria: Return improves with Sharpe near Track A and stress unchanged.
kill_criteria: Reject if beta explains nearly all incremental return.

hypothesis: Stronger offense scaling tests the mandate boundary.
success_criteria: CAGR near 9% with max drawdown above -22%.
kill_criteria: Reject if 2x costs or CVaR erase the case.

hypothesis: Combining cash reduction and mild offense boost may reach mandate with controlled stress behavior.
kill_criteria: Reject if stress or neutral-state behavior collapses.

hypothesis: Strongest Track A-timed overlay tests upper edge of drawdown tolerance.
success_criteria: CAGR >= 9% and 2x costs survive without drawdown below -22%.
kill_criteria: Reject if it is just higher beta with no benchmark edge.

hypothesis: Faster re-risking after stress exits may reduce cash drag.
success_criteria: Improves recovery_confirmed/recovery_fragile metrics without stress damage.
kill_criteria: Reject if benefit is narrow and not robust.

hypothesis: Higher offense should be disabled during high realized SPY volatility.
success_criteria: Retains much of aggressive return with better tail behavior.
kill_criteria: Reject if it gives up return without meaningful risk control.

hypothesis: Aggressive weights may survive costs if small weekly changes are ignored.
success_criteria: 2x and 3x cost sensitivity improves versus unbanded overlay.
kill_criteria: Reject if banding worsens timing more than it saves cost.

hypothesis: A simple explicit risk budget may explain return gain versus timing.
success_criteria: Improves return with acceptable drawdown and transparent beta attribution.
kill_criteria: Reject if a simple benchmark dominates it.

hypothesis: A more aggressive static blend tests whether 9-10% is mainly beta.
success_criteria: CAGR >= 9%, drawdown above -22%, and not dominated by aggressive benchmarks.
kill_criteria: Reject if return comes mostly from equity beta or drawdown exceeds mandate.
